newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 8.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading.

* The Philippine stock market, which went into a tailspin on Monday, is expected to ignore the overnight 29-point rise of the Dow Jones. "The market may likely remain weak for the rest of the week," BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said.
Yap said the selldown on Philippine property and banking issues on Monday was "overdone."
In an advisory to clients, BPI Securities pegged initial market support at the 2,900 level.
* Pryce Securities Inc said the market may likely mount a rebound today after six-straight sessions of losses.
Rise in the local treasury bill rates at Monday's auction may keep some funds in the stockmarket, it said in a commentary.
The brokerage firm attributed the drop in Philippine stock prices in the past several days due to a shift by foreign funds from equities to fixed-income securities in the region.
*The Philippine composite index ended down by 69.63 points to 2,990.96 on Monday.
*The Philippine peso fell to 26.368 at the close on Monday from 26.365 as it was pulled down by the outflow of overseas funds from the domestic stock market, traders said.
*The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate rose to an average of 9.583 percent at the regular weekly auction from 9.498 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
*Manila overnight money stayed firm at an average of 9.9375 percent on Monday even after substantial cash was drained by the Central Bank's dollar sales last week, dealers said.
*Mondragon International Philippines Inc said on Monday it expected to post a net income of 201 million pesos in the first quarter of the year from 104 million pesos in the same period last year.
*Construction firm EEI Corp said on Monday it is slated to begin two new building projects.
The company told the Philippine Stock Exchange it is to sign a 730 million peso contract for the construction of the substructure of the twin tower RCBC Plaza in Manila's Makati business district.
EEI also said it will start the construction of the foundation and structure of the 48-storey Philamlife Tower. The project is estimated to cost two billion pesos.
